formula: N = (n1+1)(n2+1)/(m+1) - 1; Var = (n1+1)(n2+1)(n1-m)(n2-m) / ((m+1)^2 (m+2)); 95% interval = N +- 1.96 SE, never below the bugs already seen.
matching_rule: Matched by bug, not by wording: two rows match when the same defect (same wrong behaviour from the same missing or wrong rule) is in both lists. A second phrasing of the same defect inside one hunter list is counted once for that hunter.

how_rough: Very rough. The overlap m is 1 (strict) or 2 (lenient). With m this small Chapman is unstable: the standard error is about as large as the estimate itself (strict 71 +- 35, lenient 47 +- 18), and moving one match changes N by 24.

The two hunters were not independent. They had the same brief and the same code, and found the same kind of bug (a closed word list, a substring match). Shared habits make the same bugs easy for both, which pushes m up and N down, so the true number is probably larger than the estimate.

Bugs are not equally easy to find (the heterogeneity problem). Easy bugs are found by both, hard bugs by neither, so Chapman is a lower-leaning guess of what a hunt of this kind can find, not of every bug in the area.
Sizes are small (11 each), and what counts as the same bug is a judgement call; the strict and lenient figures show how much that call matters.

N means bugs of the kind these two hunts can reach in the Jarvis understanding brief, about 20 seen so far. It is not a count of all defects in the app, and it says nothing about areas no hunter looked at.
Read it as: at least 20 seen; probably tens more of this kind remain (rough range 25 to 50 unseen); do not stop on a count.
